scenario.title: CRIMEAN OFFENSIVE - 7 MAY 1944
intro.text:
CRIMEAN OFFENSIVE - 7 MAY 1944

East of Sevastopol, Crimea peninsula

You're honored to liberate our beloved Sevastopol. The Germans and Romanians have already started evacuation by sea. Don't let a single man escape across the sea!

ORDERS
a. Capture all VH!
b. Prevent that more than 4 enemy ground (naval) units reach the Exit Points.

NOTES
Attention summer conditions! Don't forget to switch back to wheeled movement, if wanted.
player.speaker: Commander
line.reaction-briliant.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.reaction-briliant.text: Zhytomyr and Berdychiv fell in a breakthrough that never allowed the Fourth Panzer Army to settle. Civilian guides reached some junctions before our reconnaissance.
line.reaction-victory.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.reaction-victory.text: The region beyond Zhytomyr is open and the enemy is withdrawing. Every liberated road now carries troops west and families returning east.
line.reaction-tactical.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.reaction-tactical.text: The objectives around Zhytomyr were taken, but the breakthrough narrowed before it became a pursuit. We liberated ground faster than we restored its roads.
line.callback-choice-a.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.callback-choice-a.text: The narrow rupture at Berdychiv carried the mobile group farther than the broad-front advocates thought support could follow. The coastal plan assumes we can repeat that reach beside the sea.
line.callback-choice-b.speaker: Sergei Volkov
line.callback-choice-b.text: The broad advance beyond Zhytomyr left no liberated district hanging from one road. Here the evacuation clock may punish the same care.
line.scene-0.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.scene-0.text: Through binoculars the harbour is a forest of masts, smoke, and demolition fires. The road to Sevastopol is defended; the roads away from it are crowded. Every hour changes which target matters most.
line.scene-1.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.scene-1.text: Intercepts show German staffs reserving the first ships and Romanian units being told there is room for everyone. If the coast stays open, that promise will collapse long before their defence does.
line.decision.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.decision.text: We can drive directly for the city and its political weight, or send mobile groups to the coast first and risk slowing the main assault while the evacuation routes are sealed.
line.decision.choice.seal-the-coast.text: Send mobile groups past the city approaches to cut the embarkation roads first.
line.decision.choice.seal-the-coast.hint: Attach an eight-strength reconnaissance-infantry detachment with 50 experience and fully refuel the core; coastal transport costs 60 prestige.
line.decision.choice.take-sevastopol-fir: Concentrate on the fortified approaches and break into Sevastopol before dividing the force.
Attach an eight-strength assault-infantry detachment with 50 experience and fully replenish ammunition; siege equipment costs 60 prestige.
line.choice-a-0.speaker: Pavel Antonov
line.choice-a-0.text: The coastal groups receive the fastest vehicles and no permission to become involved in the city fight. Their objectives are roads, piers, and time.
line.choice-a-1.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.choice-a-1.text: The city will hear that mobile groups passed its outskirts while the occupation continued. Seal the coast quickly, Commander. Political explanations do not shorten a night under shellfire.
line.choice-b-0.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.choice-b-0.text: The city defence is the hinge. Break it with every gun available, then turn the released formations toward the coast before evacuation becomes escape.
line.choice-b-1.speaker: Anna Sokolova
line.choice-b-1.text: Then I will keep the embarkation reports on this table while the city guns fire. Every ship that leaves is part of the price, not an intelligence footnote.
line.post-0.speaker: Nikolai Orlov
line.post-0.text: Give the harbour reports to the city staff and the city reports to the coastal groups. No one gets to say the other road was invisible.
